key: Sharpen this song of him who strives his utmost, sharpen, God Varuna, his strength and insight; May we ascend the ship that bears us safely, whereby we may pass over all misfortune.
s: The last of three verses to Varuna, who propped the heavens, prays for the singer before the hymn turns to the Asvins; Sāyaṇa, commentary on 8.42.3, reads the ship as the sacrifice, the means of crossing the sea of suffering.

evidence.words: यया नावा यज्ञरूपया "विश्वा सर्वाणि "दुरिता दुरितानि “अति “तरेम तां “सुतर्माणं सुष्ठु तारयित्रीं यज्ञरूपां “नावम् "अधि “रुहेम वयमारुहेम । दुःखसागरतरणे हेतुत्वाद्यज्ञो नौरित्यत्र व्यपदिश्यते ॥
evidence.gloss: The ship in the form of the sacrifice, by which we may cross beyond all troubles: may we climb aboard that ship, which carries well across, the sacrifice. Because it is the cause of crossing the ocean of suffering, the sacrifice is here called a ship.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, 8.42.3 at [661,3]). The Sanskrit verse in the packet (imāṃ dhiyaṃ ... sutarmāṇam adhi nāvaṃ ruhema) is the app’s 8.42.3. Sāyaṇa glosses the ship as yajñarūpā, the sacrifice, and closes: duḥkhasāgarataraṇe hetutvād yajño naur ity atra vyapadiśyate, exactly the reading given. Plain sense is faithful: 8.42.1 to 3 are the Varuna triplet (Sāyaṇa’s preface: the first tṛca to Varuṇa, the second to the Aśvins), verse 1 tells of propping the heavens, and 4 to 6 turn to the Asvins; no four-word run from the key. Revision year 2019 confirmed by the wiki API timestamp. Entry-check ok.
